# 1 Enoch Chapter 48 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 48:3 — Pre-existence formula — translation of the key verse

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "Yea, before-the-sun and-the-signs were-created, before-the-stars of-the-heaven were-made, his-name was-named before-the-Lord of-Spirits" | Fully literal; "Yea" for emphatic particle |
| LOGOS | "Yes, before the sun and the signs were created, before the stars of heaven were made, his name was named before the Lord of Spirits" | Same; "Yes" modernizes "Yea" |
| PNEUMA | "Even before the sun and the heavenly signs were created, before the stars were set in place — his name was already named before the Lord of Spirits" | Adds emphasis; inserts dash for rhetorical force |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "Yes, before the sun and the signs were created, before the stars of heaven were made, his name was named before the Lord of Spirits" (LOGOS). The Ge'ez emphatic particle is well rendered by "Yes." PNEUMA's additions ("Even," "already," the dash) are reasonable but unsupported by the text.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. This verse is too theologically significant to add interpretive glosses.

---

## 48:4 — "light of the Gentiles" vs. "light of the nations"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "the-light of-the-Gentiles" | Traditional KJV rendering of goyim/ʾammā |
| LOGOS | "the light of the nations" | More accurate; "Gentiles" has ethnic loading |
| PNEUMA | "the light of the nations" | Agrees with LOGOS |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "The light of the nations" (LOGOS/PNEUMA). This phrase directly echoes Isa 42:6 and 49:6, where the Hebrew goyim and the Greek ethnē are properly rendered "nations" in modern translations. "Gentiles" imports a Jewish-vs.-Gentile distinction that may not be the focus here.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS/PNEUMA.

---

## 48:4 — "staff" vs. "support" — the righteous lean on him

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "a-staff to-the-righteous whereon-to-stay-themselves" | Literal; Ge'ez ʾasot = staff/walking stick |
| LOGOS | "a staff to the righteous whereon to stay themselves" | Same |
| PNEUMA | "the support on which the righteous lean" | Interprets the function |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "A staff to the righteous whereon to stay themselves and not fall" (LOGOS). "Staff" is the specific Ge'ez image and connects to OT shepherd/messianic imagery. "Support" (PNEUMA) is too generic.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 48:10 — "his Anointed" vs. "his Anointed One"

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "His-Anointed" | Literal; Ge'ez masīḥu = his anointed |
| LOGOS | "his Anointed" | Same without capitalization variation |
| PNEUMA | "his Anointed One" | Adds "One" for English idiom |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** "His Anointed" (LOGOS). The Ge'ez simply says masīḥu — literally "his anointed." "One" is unnecessary. Both forms are used in English; the shorter form is more literal and matches the usage in Ps 2:2 ("the LORD and his Anointed").

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

**Total disagreements: 4**
